about.text: A 'washable' form of distemper, the chalk-based matt finish used on British plaster walls and ceilings from the mid-18th century. Ordinary distemper is bound with animal glue and rubs off easily. Adding casein, a by-product of cheesemaking, as a binder made the finish more durable.

links.name: Designing Buildings Wiki (quoting Historic Scotland, Interior Paint)

how.text: Distemper is a water-based wall paint of chalk bound by a protein. Using casein rather than animal glue gives the harder, more wear-resistant kind; cold-water paint powders of casein, lime and filler were mixed with water on site.
